1.

Heard Ms. Ruchita Jain, learned counsel appearing for the applicant, Sri Raunak Chaturvedi,
learned counsel for the opposite party no.2, Sri Shashi Dhar Pandey learned A.G.A. for the State and perused the record.
2.

The instant application has been filed seeking quashing of the charge-sheet dated 16-09-2022,
cognizance/summoning order dated 23-01-2023 as well as entire proceedings of Criminal Case No.950 of 2023 (State Vs. Nishi Agarwal and Others), arising out of case crime no. 148 of 2021,
under Sections 420, 467, 468, 471, 406, 504, 506 IPC, P.S. Sipri Bazar, district Jhansi, pending in Smt. Nishi Agarwal vs State Of U.P. And Another on 16 February, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/130696960/

sentences.text: 3. Learned counsel for the applicant submits that in the instant case the opposite party no.2 has lodged an F.I.R. against the applicant, his husband Neeraj Agarwal and Dinesh Agarwal, father of Neeraj Agrawal with an allegation that the opposite party no.2 works as a contractor in a firm where Dinesh Kumar Agarwal, his wife Nishi Agrawal and his son Neeraj Agrawal are partners.

The firm deals with the contract of loading, unloading and transportation of foodgrains from R.F.C., F.C.I.
etc.

The opposite party no.2 had worked for the aforesaid firm and spent about Rs. 80 lacs but Neeraj Agarwal and his father Dinesh Agarwal had not paid Rs. 80 lacs which was outstanding dues and when he demanded his money back, the accused hurled abuses and threatened to kill him.

It is further submitted by the learned counsel for the applicant that Neeraj Agarwal had taken copy of the Aadhar Card and photograph of the opposite party no.2 and get him registered as a partner in a Chit Fund Society.
Further submission is that the contents of the F.I.R. clearly shows that no role has been assigned to the applicant Smt. Nishi Agrawal.
4. In the statement under Section 161 Cr.

P.C. the opposite party no.2 stated that earlier a partnership firm was registered in the name of M/S Dinesh Kumar Agarwal State Warehouse Corporation Limited in Jhansi, in which Dinesh Kumar Agarwal, Nishi Agarwal and Neeraj Agarwal were the partners.

entities.text: Dinesh Kumar Agarwal State Warehouse Corporation Limited
entities.label: ORG

sentences.text: It has further been alleged that Dinesh Kumar Agarwal, Nishi Agarwal and Neeraj Agarwal had asked the Aadhar Card and photo of the opposite party no.2 and by using his forged signature got a firm registered with State Warehouse Corporation Limited.

He further submitted that when he was going to his house, on the crossing of the road Dinesh Kumar Agarwal, Nishi Agarwal and Neeraj Agarwal met and when he asked for Rs. 80 lacs, all of three started abusing him.
5.

Thereafter another statement under Section 161 Cr.P.C. was recorded on 23-09-2021 in which the opposite party no.2 has stated that he had missed out the information that the named accused had used my documents and made forged signature to get a partnership M/S Shanker Transport Corporation registered with State Warehouse Corporation.
In both the statements no specific role has been assigned to the present applicant.
6. Learned counsel for the applicant further submits that the applicant is a housewife and has a disabled son and she spent full time, taking care off of her son.
She is not aware of any kind of business dealing and all the business dealings were done by her husband and his father.

He further submits that there was some payment dispute wherein the opposite party no.2 claims to have completed work in 2018 and was asking him to pay Rs. 80 lacs and when the same was not paid and even after the limitation period expired, the only way he could find was to file false and frivolous cases to recover the said amount.
7.

Learned counsel for the applicant further submits that the opposite party no.2 has been continuously filing first information report one after another and infact four F.I.Rs have been filed against the applicant.
The details of the F.I.Rs are hereunder:-

( i) The brother of the opposite party No.2 namely Virendra Kumar Sahu had lodged a First Information Report dated 17.11.2018 registered as Case Crime (FIR) No.1359 of Smt. Nishi Agarwal vs State Of U.P. And Another on 16 February, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/130696960/
2 2018, under Section 420, 323, 504, 506, 387 I.P.C., Police Station Sipri Bazar Lalitpur, District - Lalitpur with the similar allegations.

entities.text: Case Crime (FIR) No.1359 of Smt. Nishi Agarwal vs State Of U.P. And Another
entities.label: PRECEDENT

entities.text: Police Station Sipri Bazar Lalitpur, District -
entities.label: ORG

sentences.text: In this case charge sheet has been submitted and trial is pending.
However, the applicant has been granted interim relief from this Hon'ble Court.
Thereafter the applicant has been granted bail by the Court below.

For the kind perusal of the Hon'ble Court, a photostat copy of the First Information Report dated17.11.2018 lodged by the brother of the opposite party No.2 along with order of this Hon'ble Court is being annexed herewith and marked as Annexure No.10 to this affidavit.

(ii) Not only aforesaid case, the opposite party No.2 had also lodged a First Information Report dated 16.07.2019 registered as Case Crime No.417 of 2019, under Section 506,504, 452, 386, 420 I.P.C., Police Station Kotwali, District - Jhansi.
In this case, while submitting the charge sheet, the Investigating Officer has struck-off the name of the applicant.
For the kind perusal of this Hon'ble Court, copies of relevant documents relating to Case Crime No.417 of 2019 are being annexed herewith and marked as Annexure No.11 to this affidavit.

(iii) Thereafter the opposite party No.2 has also lodged another First Information Report dated27.11.2020 registered as Case Crime No.575of 2020, under Section 506,
504, 387, 148,147 I.P.C., Police Station Sipri Bazar,District - Jhansi.
In this case the police has submitted the final report.

For the kind perusal of this Hon'ble Court,
copies of relevant documents relating to Case Crime No.575 of 2020 are being annexed herewith and marked as Annexure No.12 to this affidavit.
(iv) The opposite party No.2 had also lodged an First Information Report registered as Case Crime No.47/2023, under Section 504, 506I.P.C., Police Station Sipri Bazar District Jhansi.

entities.text: Police Station Sipri Bazar District Jhansi
entities.label: ORG

sentences.text: In this case the investigation is pending.
For the kind perusal of this Honble Court, copies of relevant documents relating to Crime No.47/2023 are being annexed herewith and marked as Annexure No.13 to this affidavit.
8. Per contra, Sri Raunak Chaturvedi appears and submits that the accused persons on the basis of forged signature got a forged partnership registered and partnership deed was fabricated.
9. On being questioned why four F.I.Rs. were lodged against the applicant, he had no answer but the only response given is that the last F.I.R. impugned herein is against the forgery.
On being further asked how the forgery has been committed by the present applicant Nishi Agarwal, he submits that Nishi Agarwal was the beneficiary of the entire transactions.
On being asked how she was beneficiary, no possible answer was given by the learned counsel for the opposite party no.2.
He further submits that by means of a forged partnership deed Nishi Agarwal made the opposite party no.2, 51 per cent share holders of the partnership firm.
If somebody had to cheat and make a benefit why would any person give a 51 per cent of the partnership to the other party.
He further submits that there is no specific role against Nishi Agarwal and common and general role has been assigned against Nishi Agarwal, Neeraj Agarwal and Dinesh Agarwal.

He further submits that the veracity of the allegations may not be examined in an application u/s 482 Cr.P.C., however, he fails to prove Smt. Nishi Agarwal vs State Of U.P. And Another on 16 February, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/130696960/
3 any specific averment or allegation against the present applicant Nishi Agarwal.

entities.text: Smt. Nishi Agarwal vs State Of U.P. And Another
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: He further submits that it is a pure disputed questions of fact and cannot be looked into an application u/s 482 Cr.P.C..

He further submitted that the role of the Court under Section 482 Cr.P.C. is very restricted and it is only sparingly that the court should use an inherent power under Section 482 Cr.P.C. and this is not a case where the Court should exercise the inherent power.

Learned counsel for the opposite party no.2 has placed reliance on para 102 of State of Haryana Vs. Bhajan Lal 1992 Supp (1) SCC 335,
which is quoted hereunder:-
"102.

entities.text: State of Haryana Vs. Bhajan Lal 1992 Supp (1) SCC 335
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
In the backdrop of the interpretation of the various relevant provisions of the Code under Chapter XIV and of the principles of law enunciated by this Court in a series of decisions relating to the exercise of the extraordinary power under Article 226 or the inherent powers under Section 482 of the Code which we have extracted and reproduced above, we give the following categories of cases by way of illustration wherein such power could be exercised either to prevent abuse of the process of any court or otherwise to secure the ends of justice, though it may not be possible to lay down any precise, clearly defined and sufficiently channelised and inflexible guidelines or rigid formulae and to give an exhaustive list of myriad kinds of cases wherein such power should be exercised:
(1) Where the allegations made in the first information report or the complaint, even ifthey are taken at their face value and accepted in their entirety do not prima facie constitute any offence or make out a case against the accused 2) Where the allegations in the first information report and other materials, if any,
accompanying the FIR do not disclose a cognizable offence, justifying an investigation by police officers under Section 156(1) of the Code except under an order of a Magistrate within the purview of Section 155(2) of the Code.
(3) Where the uncontroverted allegations made in the FIR or complaint and the evidence collected in support of the same do not disclose the commission of any offence and make out a case against the accused.

(4) Where, the allegations in the FIR do not constitute a cognizable offence but constitute only a non-cognizable offence, no investigation is permitted by a police officer without an order of a Magistrate as contemplated under Section 155(2) of the Code.

(5) Where the allegations made in the FIR or complaint are so absurd and inherently improbable on the basis of which no prudent person can ever reach a just conclusion that there is sufficient ground for proceeding against the accused 6) Where there is an express legal bar engrafted in any of the provisions of the Code or the Act concerned (under which a criminal proceeding is instituted) to the institution and continuance of the proceedings and/or where there is a specific Smt. Nishi Agarwal vs State Of U.P. And Another on 16 February, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/130696960/
4 provision in the Code or the Act concerned, providing efficacious redress for the grievance of the aggrieved party.

entities.text: Nishi Agarwal vs State Of U.P. And Another
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: (7) Where a criminal proceeding is manifestly attended with mala fides and/or where the proceeding is maliciously instituted with an ulterior motive for wreaking vengeance on the accused and with a view to spite him due to private and personal grudge.'
10. It is apparent that the applicant is a housewife and has no active role in the business.
The opposite party no.2 evidently has a dispute where he was claiming Rs. 80 lacs which was due from the husband and his father since 2018.
Instead of filing a civil suit or suit for recovery the opposite party no.2 chose to file several F.I.Rs. just to put a pressure on the applicant's side.

In all the F.I.Rs.
the opposite party no.2 has made the applicant as an accused.

There were four F.I.Rs. filed on 17-11-2018, 16-07-2019, 27-11-2020 and 15-02-2023 and thereafter the fifth F.I.R. from which the instant proceedings arise has been filed on 11-03-2021.
11.

Hon'ble Supreme Court in the matter of Vijay Kumar Ghai and Others Vs. State of West Bengal (2022) 7 Supreme Court Cases 124 has held that :-
" ..15

entities.text: Vijay Kumar Ghai and Others Vs. State of West Bengal (2022) 7 Supreme Court Cases 124
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: A two-Judge Bench of this Court in Krishna Lal Chawla v. State of U.P. (2021) 5 SCC 435 observed that multiple complaints by the same party against the same accused in respect of the same incident is impermissible.

entities.text: Krishna Lal Chawla v. State of U.P. (2021) 5 SCC 435
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: it held that permitting multiple complaints by the same party in respect of the same incident, whether it involves a cognizable or private complaint offence, will lead to the accused being entangled in numerous criminal proceedings.
As such he would be forced to keep surrendering his liberty and precious time before the police and the courts as and when required in each case.

16. The legality of the second FIR was extensively discussed by this Court in T.T.
Antony v. State of Kerala (2001) 6 SCC 181.

entities.text:
T.T.
Antony v. State of Kerala (2001) 6 SCC 181
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: It was held that there can be no second FIR where the information concerns the same cognizable offence alleged in the first FIR or the same occurrence or incident which gives rise to one or more cognizable offences.

17. A two-Judge Bench of this Court in K. Jayaram v. BDA 2021 SCC Online 1194 observed:
" 14.

entities.text: K. Jayaram v. BDA 2021 SCC Online 1194
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
It is necessary for us to state here that in order to check multiplicity of proceedings pertaining to the same subject-matter and more importantly to stop the menace of soliciting inconsistent orders through different judicial forums by suppressing material facts either by remaining silent or by making misleading statements in the pleadings in order to escape the liability of making a false statement, we are of the view that the parties have to disclose the details of all legal proceedings and litigation either past or present concerning any part of the Smt. Nishi Agarwal vs State Of U.P. And Another on 16 February, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/130696960/
5 subject-matter of dispute which is within their knowledge.

entities.text: Nishi Agarwal vs State Of U.P. And Another
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
In case, according to the parties to the dispute, no legal proceedings or court litigation were or are pending,
they have to mandatorily state so in their pleadings in order to resolve the dispute between the parties in accordance with law."
12.
Apparently from the reading of the impugned F.I.R., 161 statement, no specific role has been assigned to the present applicant.
The allegations made are general in nature.
It is evident that the opposite party no.2 had been abusing the process of law by filing a false and frivolous cases just to settle the monetary scores between the parties.
13. Apparently no prima facie case is made out by a plain reading of the instant F.I.R. and 161 statement against the applicant.

Accordingly the instant 482 application is allowed the aforesaid proceedings of Criminal Case No.950 of 2023 (State Vs. Nishi Agarwal and Others), arising out of case crime no. 148 of 2021, under Sections 420, 467, 468, 471, 406, 504, 506 IPC, P.S. Sipri Bazar,
district Jhansi, pending in the court of Chief Judicial Magistrate, Jhansi qua Nishi Agrawal is quashed.
Order Date :- 16.2.2024/pks  Smt. Nishi Agarwal vs State Of U.P. And Another on 16 February, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/130696960/
